fields.summary: Add Moodle 5.3.0 upgrade line to all the upgrade.php scripts

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
To have it properly detected for the future, it would be great to add to all the upgrade.php scripts some lines like these:

{code:php}// Automatically generated Moodle v5.3.0 release upgrade line.
// Put any upgrade step following this.{code}

exactly before the "{{return true;}}" present in all the scripts.

Normally, it's ok to do that both in the stable (503_STABLE) and the {{main}} branches, so they will allow quickly find where 5.3.0 started and act once we decide future requirements.

But, *when under parallel development, this only can be done in the stable (503_STABLE) branch* as the {{main}} branch already has diverged and can have own upgrade steps not corresponding to the version just released, but to the future version being developed in parallel.

The change can be performed globally with:

{code:java}#!/bin/bash
export rel="5.3.0" && find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | \
grep '/db/' | \
xargs grep -L "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
xargs perl -p -i -e 's@( *)(return true;)@\1// Automatically generated Moodle v$ENV{rel} release upgrade line.\n\1// Put any upgrade step following this.\n\n\1\2@s'{code}

*Command to detect* all the upgrade.php files not having those lines:

{code:java}find . -name upgrade.php | xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | grep '/db/' | xargs grep -L 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.3.0 release upgrade'{code}

*Commands to detect* that we have not added the lines to incorrect files:

{code:java}grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.3.0 release upgrade' * | grep -v '/db/'
grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.3.0 release upgrade' * | xargs grep -L 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade'{code}

*Command to detect* if the lines have been added after a post-release upgrade step. If there are upgrade steps found, verify that all of them were already there the day of the release and have not been introduced later (you can look for differences between the release v5.3.0 and the current {{main}} branch to verify that)

{code:java}export rel="5.3.0" && export ver="202610" &&
find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -B25 "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
grep "upgrade_.*_savepoint.*${ver}"{code}

*Important note to integrators*: The sooner this issue is integrated after release, the fewer chances to get the lines put in an incorrect place (that's what the last "command to detect" above tries to avoid. We need to ensure that the lines are *exactly* at the release point (or we may end up deleting upgrade steps incorrectly in the future). So, immediate integration after release (within the on-sync period and ideally before any new upgrade step is added), it the best achievement.

Ciao 🙂

fields.summary: core/string: Handle failed string fetches in String and stringUtils

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: JavaScript
components.description: Anything related to Javascript infrastructure. Specific JS scripts should be handled by the component that the code is in.

fields.description:
Since MDL-88762, {{core/str}} forwards to {{stringUtils}}, so a failed string fetch rejects the promise that String passes to {{use()}}. The original {{AE-155}} decision assumed {{core/str}} would handle errors, so nothing does.

Reproduced in Jest with a real {{invalidparameter}} response from the get string web service:

# One bad request fails every string in the same batch.
# The rejected promise stays cached, so it never retries until the page reloads.
# With no error boundary, React 19 unmounts the whole root, not just the failed string.

Suggested fix: drop rejected promises from the string caches, and give String an error boundary that shows its fallback text.

fields.summary: Customised referenced objects in the OpenAPI specification reuse the default component

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: REST API
components.description: All work on the REST API interface

fields.description:
h3. Problem

In the router's OpenAPI generation, {{\core\router\schema\openapi_base::get_openapi_schema()}} registers any {{referenced_object}} as a shared component and returns a {{$ref}}. The reference name is derived solely from the class name.

When a route customises a referenced object, for example {{new path_user(name: 'userId')}} (the default name is {{user}}), the first instance registered wins the component name. Every later instance, whatever its customisation, produces a {{$ref}} to the first one. The generated specification therefore describes the wrong parameter name ({{user}} rather than {{userId}}) for the customised route.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Define a route using {{new path_user()}} with the default name, and another with {{new path_user(name: 'userId')}}.
# Generate the OpenAPI specification.
# Both routes reference {{#/components/parameters/core--router--parameters--path_user}}, which has {{name: user}}.

h3. Expected

A customised instance should be described by its own component, so the specification reflects the customised name.

h3. Proposed fix

* The default instance keeps the plain class-based component name, so existing references do not change.
* Any instance whose description differs from a default instance of the class is registered under a variant name, suffixed with a short hash of its description.
* The result must not depend on the order in which instances are registered.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Default and renamed {{path_user}} instances produce different {{$ref}} values, and each component carries its own {{name}}.
* The default {{$ref}} is the same whichever instance is registered first.
* Existing default {{$ref}} names are unchanged.

fields.summary: Course page main column loses width to padding that is only needed when a drawer is closed

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
h2. User goal

See as much of the course content as the screen allows, without wasted space between the drawers and the course content.

A. With the 3rem padding on {{#page.drawers}}:

!Screenshot from 2026-10-19 19-57-02-20261019-125702.png|width=959,alt="Screenshot from 2026-10-19 19-57-02-20261019-125702.png"!

B. Without the 3rem padding on {{#page.drawers}}:

!image-20261019-142515.png|width=959,alt="image-20261019-142515.png"!

h2. Figma

* [Educator-Course-page_edit-mode, 1440px|https://www.figma.com/design/KaqIUtwbetjatvzreo9wAa/MDL-89293?node-id=8037-113841]

h2. Scope

* On the course page at 768px and wider, {{#page.drawers}} reserves 3rem of padding on both sides. It keeps the content clear of the floating drawer toggle buttons.
* The padding is only needed on a side where its drawer is closed. When a drawer is open, the toggle button moves into the drawer, but the padding stays. It narrows {{.main-inner}} and leaves a large gap between the drawer and the section items.
* Remove the padding on the side of an open drawer, at 992px and wider. A side whose drawer is closed keeps it, so the content stays clear of that drawer's toggle button.
* With only one drawer open, the content column sits slightly closer to that drawer than before. The drawer and toggle anchors from MDL-89467 assume equal padding on both sides. Changing those anchors is not part of this ticket.
* The Figma frame is kept as a reference. This ticket does not change the drawer spacing to match it.

h3. Expected behaviour (at 1440px)

|| ||Today||*Proposed*||
|Padding between a drawer and {{.main-inner}}, drawer open|48px|*0px*|
|Padding on a side whose drawer is closed|48px|*48px, unchanged*|
|{{.main-inner}} width, both drawers open|About 744px|*Increased by the removed padding*|
|{{.main-inner}} width, one drawer open (below about 1250px)|Reduced by padding on both sides|*Increased by the removed padding*|
|Space from drawer edge to section items, both drawers open|About 72px left, 78px right|*Reduced by the removed padding*|
|{{.main-inner}} when both drawers are closed|About 830px, clear of the toggle buttons|*Unchanged*|

{{.main-inner}} is capped at 830px, so on wide screens where the cap already applies, the layout is unchanged.

h3. Out of scope

fields.summary: Remove Availability and Group mode from the activity ⋮ menu when the card already shows them

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)

fields.description:
h2. Rationale

[MDL-89320|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89320] and [MDL-89321|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89321] put the availability and group mode controls directly on every activity card in edit mode. Both settings can also be changed from the activity's ⋮ menu. That gives teachers two places that do the same thing, with two different looks, and both need maintaining.

The ⋮ menu should only offer what the card doesn't already show. When the card shows the control and the teacher can use it there, the menu doesn't need to offer it as well.

h2. Scope

*Activity ⋮ menu*

* Remove the availability item from the menu when the card shows the availability control and the teacher can change it from the card. The item appears either as the *Availability* submenu or, when there's only one value to switch to, as a single *Show* or *Hide* item. Both are removed.
* Remove *Group mode* from the menu when the card shows the group mode control and the teacher can change it from the card.
* If the card doesn't show an editable control, keep the menu item. For example, when the course forces a group mode, when the course format doesn't show these controls on its cards, or when the teacher can only see a read-only indicator. A setting must never become impossible to change.

*Out of scope*

* The section and subsection ⋮ menus. Their *Show* / *Hide* items stay as they are, because sections and subsections don't have an on-card control.
* Any change to the on-card controls themselves. [MDL-89320|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89320] and [MDL-89321|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89321] cover those.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* With a teacher in edit mode, an activity that shows the availability control on its card has no Availability, Show or Hide item in its ⋮ menu.
* An activity that shows the group mode control on its card has no Group mode item in its ⋮ menu.
* In a course with a forced group mode, the activity's ⋮ menu behaves as it does today.
* Section and subsection ⋮ menus still offer Show and Hide.

h2. Testing

# As a teacher, open a course with group mode not forced and turn on edit mode.
# Open the ⋮ menu on a forum. Confirm Availability and Group mode aren't listed.
# Turn on *Allow stealth activities* in Site administration. Repeat step 2 and confirm the Availability submenu isn't listed either.
# Open the ⋮ menu on a Text and media area. Confirm there's no Group mode item, and check the availability item matches what its card shows.
# Open the ⋮ menu on a section and on a subsection. Confirm Show and Hide are still there.
# Force a group mode in the course settings. Confirm the activity's ⋮ menu behaves as it does today.

fields.summary: Implement read and list for the user endpoint

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
h2. Parent and implementation baseline

[MDL-90030 — Implement a REST endpoint for a user|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90030]. Planning context: [AE-215|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/AE-215].

The local {{MDL-90234-main}} branch is the implementation baseline for this read slice. Its supplied built OpenAPI output has been used to update the read operations in the planning contract; other operations remain proposals. Branch implementation is not a claim that every acceptance criterion is complete or that the patch is integrated. The standard profile fields added below are required scope, not a claim that the earlier supplied build already includes them.

h2. Scope

* {{GET /user/users}}: visible users in the standard items/pagination envelope, with page, pagesize, search and firstname/lastname sorting. Apply visibility and read:self restrictions before pagination. Page starts at 1; default pagesize 25, maximum 100. Default ordering is lastname, firstname, id, with id only a tie-breaker. totalItems is null when not calculated; hasMore is determined from an extra result.
* {{GET /user/users/{userId}}}: one visible user's core and standard profile representation. Reuse {{core\router\parameters\path_user}} for current, numeric IDs, idnumber:… and username:…. Invisible users return 404.

Both routes apply Moodle capabilities/visibility alongside read:self or read scopes. Single-user GET emits ETag and supports bodyless 304 via If-None-Match. The collection has no ETag.

Include the standard profile fields city, country, institution, department, phone, mobilePhone, address, description and descriptionFormat in both read responses. They are part of the shared User representation, not a nested profile object or separate profile GET. This allows read/write consistency with MDL-90235 and MDL-90240. Custom profile fields remain out of scope for a separate future issue; account creation and mutations are also separate issues.

h2. Shared user schema

Use the same referenced {{core_user\route\schema\user_object}} for collection items and the single-user response. The planning contract calls these User and UserCollection.

||Fields||Parameter type / meaning||
|id|INT|
|username|USERNAME|
|idnumber|RAW|
|fullName, firstName, lastName, firstNamePhonetic, lastNamePhonetic, middleName, alternateName|NOTAGS|
|email|EMAIL|
|lang|LANG|
|auth|AUTH|
|confirmed, suspended, deleted|BOOL|
|profileImageUrl, profileImageUrlSmall|URL|
|profileImageAlt|TEXT|
|timeZone, timeZonePreference|TIMEZONE|
|city, institution, department, address|TEXT|
|country|ALPHA; ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code or readable empty value|
|phone, mobilePhone|NOTAGS; map to phone1 and phone2 respectively|
|description|Formatted profile description from the existing user-details API; preserve permitted formatted content rather than treating it as plain text|
|descriptionFormat|INT; content format accompanying description|

Hidden/unavailable fields are explicit nulls without disclosing why. Delegate visibility to core user-details rules; additional names follow full-name formatting/viewfullnames, account language/auth/confirmation follow self/viewalldetails, idnumber follows identity-field/self/viewalldetails rules and email follows email-display/visibility rules.

For the added standard profile fields, preserve the existing user-details capability, hidden-field, identity-field and profile-description rules, including course-context fallback. Do not copy raw user-record fields into the response to bypass these rules. Follow the existing formatted-description output and its descriptionFormat; do not strip valid formatted content or expose source markup under an incorrect format. Hidden/unavailable description and format are null. Apply the agreed response empty/null semantics consistently and document existing helper limitations rather than silently disclosing values.

lang is the stored Moodle language preference, not effective page language. auth is the configured account authentication plugin, not the current request's mechanism. confirmed is account confirmation, not a universal email-verification assertion.

timeZone is the effective IANA tz database name (BCP 175 / RFC 6557), including a forced site timezone. timeZonePreference is the normalised stored preference; null means follow the server default (stored as 99). Legacy numeric offsets are normalised, e.g. 8.0 → Etc/GMT-8. Both values are null when hidden.

firstAccess and lastAccess are excluded. Deleted users remain excluded, so returned records currently have deleted:false.

h2. Shared infrastructure and architecture

This slice supplies reusable pagination_request, collection_response/collection_object, collection and etag route attributes, and conditional_request. Later user issues reuse them rather than treating their creation as an external prerequisite.

Referenced header schemas are {{core\router\schema\parameters\etag}}, {{if_none_match}} and {{if_match}}. Preserve literal quotes in ETags. Shared parsing validates quoted entity-tags, weak prefixes, lists, quoted commas and wildcard alone; malformed values throw invalid_parameter_exception. If-None-Match uses weak comparison, If-Match strong comparison with 412 on mismatch. Reuse the precomputed response ETag.

Use thin handlers and injectable visible_user_finder/user_representation services. visible_user_finder uses {{core\dml\database_proxy}} and {{core\current_user}}; scope checks use the injected current user. Core helpers still consult global current-user state internally: arbitrary-viewer support is not promised. Set PAGE's system context before generating profile-picture URLs.

The single-user response's headers array references the reusable ETag schema. Collection response and single-user response reference the same user schema. Route classes are discovered automatically in core_user; no registration file or new user-id resolver is needed.

h2. Acceptance criteria

These are review/verification criteria; none are marked complete merely because a branch exists.

* Both GET endpoints return the documented schemas and applicable RFC 9457 errors (400 malformed input, 422 well-formed validation failures, and 401/403/404 as applicable).
* Collection visibility, search and read:self restrictions are applied before pagination and cannot leak other users through items, hasMore, totals or conditional responses.
* Validate page >= 1, pagesize 1–100 and supported sort fields; default pagesize is 25 and default order lastname, firstname, id. hasMore reflects an extra visible result; totalItems is null when not calculated.
* Identifier forms resolve consistently; invisible users return 404.
* Collection items and single-user responses share the named user schema and the complete field set above, including city, country, institution, department, phone, mobilePhone, address, description and descriptionFormat as top-level fields.
* Tests cover the added standard profile fields for self, authorised viewers and restricted viewers, including identity/hidden-field rules, readable empty values, explicit nulls and course visibility fallback. phone/mobilePhone map correctly to phone1/phone2.
* Description and descriptionFormat preserve existing formatted-output and visibility rules; tests exercise formatted content and hidden/unavailable descriptions.
* Tests cover idnumber, lang, confirmed/auth visibility, additional names and profileImageAlt; firstAccess/lastAccess and custom profile fields are absent.
* Timezone tests cover explicit IANA values, server default, legacy offsets, hidden values and forced site timezone while preserving the stored preference.
* Single-user 200 responses document ETag; matching If-None-Match returns bodyless 304 with ETag. Collection responses have no ETag. Added visible standard profile values participate in the single-user representation and ETag.
* Conditional-request tests cover quoted tags, weak/strong comparison, lists, quoted commas, wildcard, malformed syntax and invalid_parameter_exception. Precomputed ETags are reused.
* ETag/If-None-Match/If-Match are reusable referenced header components; references resolve and literal-quote guidance is visible in Swagger UI.
* Profile-image URL generation works in web requests without a pre-existing PAGE context; regression tests must not rely on CLI's silent context fallback.
* Shared collection/etag attributes, pagination_request, collection_response and conditional_request are covered by router tests and available for later slices.
* Generated OpenAPI correctly declares nullable values and required properties, including the added standard profile fields. Known gap in the earlier supplied build: User fields are plain scalars despite runtime nulls, and required-property declarations are absent.
* Collection response is a named reusable schema. Known gap: earlier built output inlines it; the planning contract extracts the same shape as UserCollection for review.
* Authentication documentation reflects supported OAuth, API-token and cookie flows. Known gap: supplied generated operations list only OAuth alternatives.
* GET responses are not persisted in idempotency replay storage; use endpoint exclusions if needed.
* CamelCase path-parameter names intentionally match {userId}; developer documentation and route/domain tests accompany implementation.
* Regenerate/update the OpenAPI review contract and examples to include the new standard profile fields in both read responses; the earlier captured build is not evidence that these additions are already implemented.

h2. Relevant implementation files

* public/user/classes/route/api/users.php
* public/user/classes/local/visible_user_finder.php
* public/user/classes/local/user_representation.php
* public/user/classes/local/user_scope_check_trait.php
* public/user/classes/route/schema/user_object.php
* public/user/classes/route/responses/user_response.php and user_collection_response.php
* public/user/classes/route/scope/user/read.php and read_self.php
* public/lib/classes/router/pagination_request.php and conditional_request.php
* public/lib/classes/router/schema/collection.php and etag.php
* public/lib/classes/router/schema/objects/collection_object.php
* public/lib/classes/router/schema/response/collection_response.php
* public/lib/classes/router/schema/parameters/etag.php, if_none_match.php and if_match.php
* public/lib/classes/current_user.php and public/lib/classes/dml/database_proxy.php
* public/user/tests/route/api/users_test.php and user_scope_test.php
* public/lib/tests/router/collection_test.php and conditional_request_test.php

h2. Style-guide alignment, blockers and related work

Retain the existing dependencies on [MDL-90104|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90104], [MDL-89850|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-89850], [moodle/devdocs#1732|https://github.com/moodle/devdocs/pull/1732] and [MDLSITE-7035|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDLSITE-7035]. Follow their agreed guidance, particularly response nullability and the 400/422 boundary. AE-213 remains related non-blocking idempotency work.

Related write slices: [MDL-90235|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90235] and [MDL-90240|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90240]. Custom-field work is a separate future issue.

fields.description:
h2. Parent and scope

[MDL-90030 — Implement a REST endpoint for a user|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90030].

Implement {{PATCH /user/users/{userId}}} to update supplied account and standard profile fields and return the updated MDL-90234 User representation with ETag. Omitted fields remain unchanged. No PUT or separate standard-profile endpoint is added.

Account creation is [MDL-90240|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90240]. Custom profile fields are *out of scope*, including customFields payloads, validation, storage and shared custom-field services; a new separate issue will cover them. Password changes/resets are separate endpoints. Do not copy the broader AE-215 prototype wholesale.

h2. Request fields

Use a named UserUpdate schema with additionalProperties:false and minProperties:1. Extend writable account fields to cover the writable fields exposed by the MDL-90234-main read implementation, excluding deleted. Retain the existing standard profile inputs.

||Writable field||Type / meaning||
|username|USERNAME; site policy and uniqueness rules|
|idnumber|RAW; account identifier|
|firstName, lastName|NOTAGS; validate required account names|
|firstNamePhonetic, lastNamePhonetic, middleName, alternateName|NOTAGS|
|email|EMAIL; site email and uniqueness policy|
|lang|LANG; stored Moodle language preference (not language)|
|auth|AUTH; supported account authentication plugin|
|confirmed|BOOL; account confirmation, not universal email verification|
|suspended|BOOL; suspension invalidates active sessions|
|profileImageAlt|TEXT; maps to imagealt, not an image upload|
|timeZonePreference|IANA timezone string, or null to follow the server default|
|city, institution, department, address, description|Strings, following existing user-field validation|
|country|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or empty where supported|
|phone, mobilePhone|Strings mapping to phone1 and phone2|

Read-only: id, fullName, profileImageUrl, profileImageUrlSmall and timeZone. fullName is computed; picture URLs do not provide an upload API; timeZone is the effective zone including site policy. deleted is not writable and is not an update input. Unknown/read-only inputs are rejected rather than ignored.

Use timeZonePreference for writes, not timeZone. A null preference maps to Moodle's server-default sentinel (99), but the API must not expose/accept 99 as a timezone name. An explicit value must be a supported IANA tz database name. A forced site timezone may make the effective timeZone differ from the stored preference; preserve both meanings in the returned representation. Omitted preference remains unchanged.

Null is otherwise rejected; clear optional text with an empty string. Preserve existing required-field and validation rules. At least one writable property is required. Standard profile fields retain their existing contract; their presence here does not add custom fields or silently change the MDL-90234 response field set.

h2. Permissions and lifecycle

* Require Moodle capabilities as well as {{core_user:user:update}} or {{core_user:user:update:self}}; self scope only permits the caller's account.
* Email and suspension require moodle/user:update even for self. Administrative account changes (username, idnumber, auth, confirmed) must not become permitted merely by having a self-update scope; enforce Moodle's applicable account-edit rules and capabilities, including moodle/user:update for these administrative changes.
* Apply existing field-level/self-edit permissions to names, language, image alt, timezone preference and standard profile fields. Enforce authentication-plugin locks with 403; changing auth must not bypass source/target plugin constraints or provision an external identity.
* Changing confirmed follows the normal account-confirmation lifecycle; it is not an arbitrary email-verification operation. No implicit password set/reset is introduced through auth changes.
* Use existing domain APIs and validation, not web service entry points. Update in a transaction, emit user_updated through the normal lifecycle, and invalidate sessions on suspension. Document validation/lifecycle differences from existing forms and web services.
* Reuse core\router\parameters\path_user for current, numeric ID, idnumber:… and username:….

h2. Conditional requests and errors

Reuse MDL-90234's etag attribute, conditional_request and referenced if_match/etag header schemas. Compare If-Match against the same caller-visible current representation used by GET before mutation. Omitted header is unconditional; non-matching strong tags return 412 and change nothing. Preserve quotes; malformed entity-tags use invalid_parameter_exception. Return the updated shared User and its ETag on success. Coordinate the check/write to avoid a concurrency race.

RFC 9457 responses: 400 malformed/uninterpretable request, 422 well-formed invalid fields with details:[{field,code,message}], 401/403/404 as applicable, 409 uniqueness conflicts, 412 failed precondition. Add/reuse a named UniquenessConflict response. PATCH is not stored for idempotent replay; retry safety is not promised by this issue.

h2. Contract and implementation

* PATCH /user/users/{userId}: named UserUpdate request, shared User success response with referenced ETag header, referenced If-Match parameter and standard errors.
* UserUpdate lists every writable field above, with no customFields property; all optional, additionalProperties:false, minProperties:1. Only timeZonePreference accepts null.
* Use lang rather than language and timeZonePreference rather than timeZone in new examples. Include names/phonetics, idnumber, auth/confirmed, language, image alt, follow-server timezone, email, suspension, standard location/organisation and clearing optional text.
* Thin users::update_user route; user_updater domain service for permissions/locks/validation/transaction/session lifecycle; extend user_scope_check_trait and add update/update_self scopes. Class names should follow repository conventions.
* Reuse MDL-90234's current_user and database_proxy injection where needed rather than capturing globals. Request and response schemas are named reusable components.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* All writable fields in the table are covered by request schemas, validation and tests; computed read fields are explicitly read-only, and deleted is excluded from inputs.
* Standard profile inputs remain supported; customFields and custom-field processing are absent and rejected as unknown input.
* Only supplied fields change; omitted fields remain unchanged. Empty bodies, unknown/read-only properties and invalid/null values return 422 with per-field details, except the supported null timezone preference.
* timeZonePreference:null selects server default; explicit IANA values persist the preference; timeZone is read-only and reflects effective site policy. No 99 sentinel leaks into the API.
* Self scope cannot alter another account or grant administrative account-edit permissions. Email/suspension and administrative identity/auth/confirmation changes enforce applicable capabilities, including moodle/user:update.
* Auth-plugin locks/constraints are enforced with 403; auth changes do not bypass password lifecycle or create external identities.
* Username/email uniqueness conflicts return 409 where required by Moodle policy; idnumber follows existing Moodle validation rather than assuming a new uniqueness guarantee.
* Stale If-Match returns 412 with no mutation; success returns the updated shared User representation and ETag. Check/write concurrency is protected appropriately.
* Suspending invalidates sessions; user_updated follows the normal lifecycle; failed field validation leaves no partial update.
* Named schemas/generated OpenAPI document types, nullability, writable/read-only distinction and errors accurately.
* Tests cover each added field, false booleans, empty optional text, default timezone, forced timezone, omitted fields, permissions/self scope, locks, conflicts, transaction failure and conditional requests.

h2. Dependencies

* MDL-90234: shared User schema, headers, conditional_request and router infrastructure.
* MDL-90104; MDL-89850; https://github.com/moodle/devdocs/pull/1732; MDLSITE-7035.
* Custom-field work is a separate future issue, not a prerequisite or a service to introduce here.

h2. Parent

[MDL-90030 — Implement a REST endpoint for a user|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90030]

h2. What to build

Create the user deletion endpoint:

* {{DELETE /user/users/{userId}}}: delete one Moodle account through Moodle's normal deletion lifecycle. Returns {{204}} with no body.

This is new work. This is ordinary account deletion, *not a complete personal-data erasure (GDPR) operation*. The [AE-215 branch|https://github.com/andrewnicols/moodle/tree/AE-215] is a proof of concept only, not an implementation to merge.

h3. Decisions and constraints

* *Lifecycle:* delegate to Moodle's existing user deletion ({{delete_user()}} or equivalent) so enrolment and role cleanup, session invalidation, events ({{user_deleted}}) and authentication-plugin notification all occur. Do not reimplement deletion and do not call the web service function.
* *Permissions:* token scope {{core_user:user:delete}}, plus system-level {{moodle/user:delete}}. There is no self-scoped delete token. Moodle capabilities always apply in addition to the scope.
* *Protected accounts:* the guest account, site administrators and the caller's own account cannot be deleted and return {{403}}. Check these before any deletion work.
* *Missing or already-deleted users* return {{404}}. Repeating a successful DELETE therefore returns {{404}}; the account stays deleted. Do not disclose the reason when the caller cannot see the user.
* *Concurrency:* optional {{If-Match}} using the ETag returned by {{GET /user/users/{userId}}}. A mismatch returns {{412}} and deletes nothing; omitting it permits unconditional deletion. Reuse the {{conditional_request}} support created by MDL-90234.
* *Identifiers:* use the existing {{\core\router\parameters\path_user}} ({{current}}, numeric ID, {{idnumber:…}}, {{username:…}}). Resolving {{current}} and then deleting it returns {{403}} as the caller's own account.
* *Errors:* RFC 9457 problem responses: {{400}} malformed request, {{422}} well-formed invalid parameters, {{401}}/{{403}}/{{404}}/{{412}} as above.
* Idempotency replay is not a design concern for this issue. DELETE is naturally repeat-safe, and a repeat returns {{404}} rather than a stored {{204}}.
* Deletion is not atomic across external systems; document that authentication-plugin notification failures follow existing {{delete_user()}} behaviour.

h3. Blockers

* [MDL-90234|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90234] — creates the shared {{conditional_request}} support and the {{User}} ETag that {{If-Match}} relies on.
* [MDL-90104|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90104]
* [MDL-89850|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-89850]
* [moodle/devdocs#1732|https://github.com/moodle/devdocs/pull/1732]
* [MDLSITE-7035|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDLSITE-7035]

h3. Relevant OpenAPI contract

Excerpt from the proposed AE-215 {{openapi.json}}:

{code:yaml}DELETE /user/users/{userId}:
  security:
    - oauth2: [core_user:user:delete]
    - api_key: []
    - cookie: []
  parameters:
    - name: userId
      in: path
      required: true
      description: Resolved by `\core\router\parameters\path_user`.
      schema: {type: string}
    - name: If-Match
      in: header
      required: false
      description: >
        Optional ETag of the user representation. A mismatch returns 412;
        omitting the header permits unconditional deletion.
      schema: {type: string}
  responses:
    '204':
      description: The user account was deleted. No response body.
    '400': {$ref: '#/components/responses/core--router--response--invalid_parameter_response'}
    '401': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthenticated'}
    '403': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden'}
    '404': {$ref: '#/components/responses/core--router--response--not_found_response'}
    '412': {$ref: '#/components/responses/core--router--response--precondition_failed_response'}
    '422': {$ref: '#/components/responses/ValidationFailure'}{code}

There are no new request or response schemas: {{204}} has no body and all error responses are existing router components.

h3. Proposed files and classes

||File||Class||Responsibility||
|{{public/user/classes/route/api/users.php}}|{{core_user\route\api\users}}|Add {{delete_user()}} for {{DELETE /user/users/{userId}}}, returning {{204}}.|
|{{public/user/classes/local/user_deleter.php}}|{{core_user\local\user_deleter}}|Enforce protected-account rules and delegate to Moodle's deletion lifecycle.|
|{{public/user/classes/route/scope/user/delete.php}}|{{core_user\route\scope\user\delete}}|Declare the user-delete token scope.|
|{{public/user/tests/route/api/users_test.php}}|{{core_user\route\api\users_test}}|Route tests for deletion.|
|{{public/user/tests/local/user_deleter_test.php}}|—|Unit tests for protected accounts, permissions and lifecycle side effects.|

Class names are proposals; align them with existing conventions during implementation.

h2. Deliverables

* {{DELETE /user/users/{userId}}} with generated OpenAPI documentation.
* Protected-account checks (guest, site administrators, own account).
* Deletion through the normal Moodle lifecycle, with optional {{If-Match}}.
* Route and unit tests.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Callers need both the {{core_user:user:delete}} scope and {{moodle/user:delete}}.
* Guest, site administrator and own-account deletion return {{403}} and delete nothing.
* Missing and already-deleted users return {{404}}; repeating a successful request returns {{404}}.
* A stale {{If-Match}} returns {{412}} and deletes nothing; a matching or omitted {{If-Match}} deletes the user.
* Success returns {{204}} with no body.
* Enrolment and role cleanup, session invalidation, {{user_deleted}} and authentication-plugin notification occur as for existing deletion.
* Documentation states that this is not personal-data erasure.
* Route and unit tests cover protected accounts, permissions, repeat requests and {{412}}.

fields.summary: Implement create for the user endpoint

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
h2. Parent and scope

[MDL-90030 — Implement a REST endpoint for a user|https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-90030].

Implement POST /user/users for administrative provisioning of one Moodle account with optional initial standard profile values. Return 201, a numeric-user Location and a non-secret creation receipt. This is not self-registration and does not create an account in an external identity provider. The AE-215 prototype is not an implementation to merge wholesale.

Custom profile fields are out of scope: remove customFields from requests, examples, validation, storage and atomicity requirements. A new separate issue will cover them; do not introduce a custom-field service or dependency here.

h2. Request fields

Use named UserCreation with additionalProperties:false. Required: username, firstName, lastName, email. Add the writable fields exposed by MDL-90234-main, excluding deleted, and retain standard profile inputs.

||Field||Type / meaning||
|username|USERNAME; required, site policy and uniqueness rules|
|firstName, lastName|NOTAGS; required|
|email|EMAIL; required, site email policy|
|idnumber|RAW|
|firstNamePhonetic, lastNamePhonetic, middleName, alternateName|NOTAGS|
|lang|LANG; stored language preference, defaults according to site policy; replaces language|
|auth|AUTH; supported authentication plugin, default manual|
|confirmed|BOOL; account confirmation, not universal email verification; apply normal administrative provisioning defaults when omitted|
|suspended|BOOL; initial account suspension state; apply normal defaults when omitted|
|profileImageAlt|TEXT; imagealt, not image upload|
|timeZonePreference|IANA timezone string or null for server default; omission follows server default|
|profile.city, profile.institution, profile.department, profile.address, profile.description|Optional standard profile strings with existing validation|
|profile.country|ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, or empty where supported|
|profile.phone, profile.mobilePhone|Standard profile strings mapping to phone1/phone2|
|password|Write-only explicit password, subject to plugin/policy rules below|
|generatePassword|Boolean, default false|
|sendPasswordEmail|Boolean, default true when generating; only valid with generatePassword:true|

Retain the existing nested profile object for initial standard profile values, with additionalProperties:false. These standard fields are not custom profile fields.

Computed/read-only fields: id, fullName, profileImageUrl, profileImageUrlSmall and effective timeZone. Reject them as inputs. deleted is excluded. Use timeZonePreference, never timeZone, to choose a stored timezone. Null maps to the internal server-default sentinel 99; do not accept 99 as a timezone name. An explicit supported IANA value persists the preference even when a forced site timezone changes the effective zone. Other null values are rejected. Unknown properties, including customFields, are rejected.

h2. Password and email rules

For authentication plugins with Moodle-managed passwords, provide either password or generatePassword:true, never both, and one is required. Explicit passwords must meet site policy and do not trigger email or forced change. Generated passwords force a change at first login and are emailed unless sendPasswordEmail:false. sendPasswordEmail is only valid with generatePassword:true. Authentication without Moodle-managed passwords rejects explicit passwords and generation. Passwords are never returned or logged.

Keep generatePassword/sendPasswordEmail in the POST body, not query parameters. Plugin selection provisions only the Moodle account; respect supported authentication/plugin rules.

h2. Permissions, atomicity and lifecycle

* Require core_user:user:create scope plus system moodle/user:create. Supplying initial fields does not require separate read/update scope; apply existing administrative provisioning permissions, validation and plugin rules.
* Validate/save account and initial standard profile fields consistently in one transaction. Failure leaves no partial account. Apply defaults and existing uniqueness/required-field rules. Initial provisioning is distinct from later plugin field locks.
* Follow the normal user creation lifecycle and emit user_created after supplied data is saved. Reuse user-domain APIs, not web service entry points.
* Send generated-credential email only after commit. Delivery failure is logged and does not undo account creation; report credentialEmailStatus. Clients must not repeat POST to retry delivery.
* No custom-field processing or service is required. Password handling remains part of creation, not ordinary user PATCH.

h2. Response and errors

201 returns named UserCreationReceipt: required id and username; credentialEmailStatus (sent, failed, notRequested) only when generatePassword:true. Location is the new user's numeric-id URL. No password or ETag is returned. An authorised GET fetches the shared User representation and ETag; the receipt requires no extra read scope.

RFC 9457 errors: 400 malformed input, 422 invalid values with details:[{field,code,message}], 401/403 as applicable and 409 username/email uniqueness conflicts where site policy requires. Reuse MDL-90235's UniquenessConflict response. Idnumber follows existing validation rather than inventing a uniqueness requirement. Do not promise idempotent POST retry safety.

h2. Contract and implementation

* Named UserCreation and UserCreationReceipt schemas, referenced errors/Location header and operation-level examples.
* Include examples for explicit passwords, external authentication, generated passwords with standard profile values, no-email provisioning, additional names/idnumber/lang/image alt/account flags and server-default timezone. Remove custom-field examples and old language/timeZone inputs.
* Thin users::create_user route, user_creator domain service, credential_provisioner for plugin/password/email policy and user/create scope. Follow repository naming conventions.
* Reuse the current_user/database_proxy services and field validation from earlier slices as appropriate.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Required fields and all optional writable fields above are implemented, documented and tested. Computed fields are explicitly read-only; deleted is not an input.
* Standard profile values remain supported; customFields is rejected and no custom-field handling/service dependency is introduced.
* Validation follows existing forms/domain APIs with documented differences; schemas accurately declare types, defaults and nullability.
* timeZonePreference supports explicit IANA values or null/server default; timeZone is not writable. Forced timezone does not overwrite the stored preference.
* The caller needs create scope and moodle/user:create; field initialization does not require a separate read/update scope.
* Both explicit/generated password options together, missing credentials for password-managed authentication, unsupported plugin credentials and sendPasswordEmail without generation return 422.
* Generated passwords force change and default to email; explicit passwords cause neither. Passwords never appear in responses/logs.
* Creation is atomic across account and standard profile values; failure leaves no account. user_created follows the normal lifecycle after supplied values are saved.
* Email failure after commit leaves the account created and reports failed; credentialEmailStatus appears only for generation.
* 201 returns numeric-id Location and non-secret receipt, with no ETag or additional read-scope requirement.
* Username/email conflicts return 409 where required. Tests cover permissions, all new fields including false booleans, timezone defaults/site policy, validation, plugins, credentials, transaction failure, lifecycle and email outcomes.

h2. Dependencies

* MDL-90234: read schema/scopes/shared router infrastructure, including standard profile fields needed for read/write consistency.
* MDL-90235: shared user-field validation and UniquenessConflict response.
* MDL-90104; MDL-89850; https://github.com/moodle/devdocs/pull/1732; MDLSITE-7035.
* Custom-field work is a separate future issue, not a prerequisite.

fields.summary: core_course_get_contents returns an empty activitybadge for modules without badge content

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
{{core_course_get_contents}} adds an {{activitybadge}} to every module whose plugin has an activity badge class (Forum, File), even when the badge has no content.

In {{public/course/externallib.php}} (around lines 292-295), {{get_activitybadge()}} returns an empty object when there is no badge content, and the result is checked with {{!empty($activitybadgedata)}}, which is always true for an object. So a Forum without unread posts, or a File with “Show type” off, gets an {{activitybadge}} with no fields.

[https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-90129|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-90129|smart-link] fixed the same pattern in the course page output ({{core_courseformat\output\local\content\cm}}).

Before changing the web service output, check with the Mobile Apps team whether the app relies on {{activitybadge}} being present.

Expected result: {{activitybadge}} is only returned when the badge has content.
